summary: This component renders an interactive terminal display with optional typewriter animation. It can display code or command-line output, let users copy the text to their clipboard, and animate the text character-by-character for command lines while showing output lines all at once. The component intelligently resolves variable substitutions, auto-scales animation speed based on content length, and only starts animating once the terminal scrolls into view.

explanations.30: HeadingPrefixMap is a TypeScript type alias defining a Map that stores React component references as keys and their corresponding markdown heading prefixes (like '# ', '## ') as string values.
explanations.32: This function recursively extracts plain text from React children, handling arrays, strings, and component elements—it needs the headingPrefixMap to prepend heading symbols like '# ' that MDX normally strips away.
explanations.40: The function recursively calls itself on each child, concatenating results and inserting separators between array items (newlines by default, but empty string inside Fragments to avoid spurious line breaks).
explanations.48: We cast the child object (which we know is a ReactElement because we checked it's an object) to the ReactElement type so TypeScript lets us access .type and .props properties.
explanations.50: We look up the element's type (like a heading component) in our headingPrefixMap to find its prefix; if not found, we default to an empty string.
explanations.52: When recursing into a Fragment's children, we switch the separator from newline to empty string because the Fragment itself contributes no line break—only its actual text content should.
explanations.61: This function returns animation timing defaults that decrease speed and delay as line count increases, so a 50-line terminal doesn't take forever to animate.
explanations.113: useMDXComponents() fetches the map of Docusaurus's registered MDX components (like h1, h2, etc.) which are anonymous functions, not string names.
explanations.114: We build a Map once (via useMemo) that lets us look up heading component functions and native HTML tag strings to their markdown prefixes, used later by getCopyText.
explanations.128: useVarResolver is a custom hook that returns a function to resolve variable markers (like %%name=default%%) to their current values.
explanations.129: We resolve any variable markers in children once and store the result; copy, animation, and rendering all use this same resolved tree so substitutions never get skipped anywhere.
explanations.142: We extract and split the full text into lines once when typewriter mode starts, capturing it at that moment so in-flight animations aren't disrupted if the user edits a variable mid-animation.
explanations.145: The exhaustive-deps rule is intentionally disabled here because we only want animLines to update when typewriter changes, not when resolvedChildren or headingPrefixMap update (which would restart the animation).
explanations.149: We compute the final animation speed, using explicit props if provided, otherwise falling back to the auto-scaled defaults based on line count.
explanations.158: This state tracks whether the terminal has ever been visible on screen, since we defer starting the animation until that happens.
explanations.168: IntersectionObserver is a browser API that fires a callback when an element scrolls into the viewport; we use it here to trigger the animation only when visible.
explanations.188: The animation loop exits early if typewriter is off, the component isn't visible yet, or the animation is already done.
explanations.197: A regex that checks if a line is a command (starts with optional whitespace followed by $ or #); command lines animate character-by-character, output lines appear whole.
explanations.199: If it's a command line and we haven't shown all characters yet, advance by one character after the specified speed delay.
explanations.205: Empty lines get a shorter pause (80ms) than output lines (which use effectiveDelay) so the timing feels natural.
explanations.223: This callback immediately skips the animation by revealing all lines at once and marking it done; it's fired when the user clicks the terminal.
explanations.230: This callback extracts the current text, writes it to the clipboard, and temporarily shows the 'copied' checkmark state.
explanations.247: We compute the partially-typed display: for animation mode, show all fully-revealed lines plus the currently-typing line truncated to charIdx characters.
explanations.249: The optional chaining (?.) prevents errors if lineIdx is out of bounds; if no line exists at that index, partial becomes an empty string.
explanations.286: The 'ghost' span invisibly renders the final content so the <pre> immediately knows its full height, preventing the page from reflowing as each animated line appears.
